releases.summary: the tagging scheme: what a tag encodes, what moves it, what it promises, and what a consumer re-verifies after re-pinning; and the writable-filesystem ruling
re_verify: nothing in a running container: this release adds keys to this contract and changes no build input, so the tag you already pinned is still the tag this checkout computes
your compose file: regenerate it from this contract, because the rendered service now states read_only explicitly
that you never mount any path in editor.filesystem.never_read_only read-only, and never set the compose read_only key true

releases.summary: the compose and mount contract, the four rulings it refuses to render against, and the entrypoint that repairs the container's uid before it seeds anything
re_verify: recompute the tag with editor.image.tag.computed_by and re-pin it: the entrypoint changed, so every editor tag moved
bring the editor up as the uid that owns your sources, and confirm a file it writes there belongs to you and not to root
that your compose file publishes the editor on editor.ports[0].host_bind and on no other address

editor.what_it_is: code-server with the runtimes a corpus declares, served to a browser on loopback

image.why_no_registry: this component has no remote and is never pushed; a consumer builds the image from this checkout and pins the tag the build prints
image.compose_value: ${EDITOR_IMAGE:?build it with docker/editor/build.py and pin the tag it prints}

parts.repository: always editor.image.repository; this component publishes one editor image and names it once
parts.set: the declared runtimes, sorted and joined with a hyphen, or the word none when the set is empty
parts.arch: the architecture the image was built for, as this component's pins name it
parts.inputs: the leading twelve characters of a hash over every build input's relative path and bytes

tag.computed_not_parsed: a set joined with hyphens cannot be split back out of the tag unambiguously, and nothing should try: ask the build for the tag, and read the set back from editor.runtimes.read_back_from on the image you pinned
moved_by: a runtime added to or removed from the declared set
a version bump in pins.json or editor-pins.json: every pinned toolchain, extension and package is a build input
an edit to any file under editor.image.tag.build_inputs, including the Dockerfile and the entrypoint
a prime directory supplied to the build, or a change to the one supplied: its digest is folded in, so an image warmed for one corpus never carries another's tag
not_moved_by: this contract file, docs/, tests/, README.md and consuming/: the consuming half is versioned by provides, not by the tag
anything on the host that built it: the build cache, the daemon, the day
promises: the declared set: the same tag always names the same runtimes, and editor.image.labels.runtimes on the image states them
the pinned versions: every toolchain, extension and package version that went into it, because each pin file is a build input
the run shape of this contract's consuming_api: what a compose file must supply does not change under a tag
does_not_promise: byte-identical images: two hosts that build the same tag ran the same pinned inputs, not the same bytes; a Docker build is not bit-reproducible and this component does not claim it is
the keys of this contract: those move with provides, which a tag does not encode. Read both
tag.why_it_cannot_be: the tag is computed from the inputs, so a changed input computes a different tag rather than overwriting one: there is no name a consumer pinned that a later build can take away. Two consumers on two sets, or on two checkouts, hold two tags and can run them at once
tag.how_to_pin: Record the tag that command prints beside the commit this component is pinned at, and set editor.image.env_var to it. Never pin a tag you did not compute and never edit one by hand: a tag is a function of the build's inputs, so a hand-made one names nothing.

upgrade.how: re-run editor.image.tag.computed_by in the new checkout and compare it with the tag you hold; when it differs, rebuild, re-pin, and work the re_verify list below and the one in the releases entry you moved to
re_verify: the set: read editor.image.labels.runtimes off the image you pinned, and confirm it is the set you declared
the contract: read provides in this file; keys may have been added since you generated your compose file, and a release entry says what they are
the run: bring your own compose file up and confirm editor.healthcheck.path answers editor.healthcheck.expect_status
the ownership: confirm a file the container writes into your sources belongs to you and not to root
upgrade.notes_per_release: the top-level releases array, newest first: one entry per change a consumer must act on, each saying whether it moved every tag

not_carried.sqlite: the runner installs it from Debian's packages into /usr/bin, and the editor copies only /opt and /usr/local out of the runner

runs_as.set_to: the uid:gid that owns the mounted sources on the host
runs_as.why: a container that runs as root writes root-owned files into the mounted sources, and the reader can then never edit their own repository
runs_as.how: the base image's fixuid repairs the passwd record and the ownership of the home directory for whatever uid the consumer ran it as; the editor's entrypoint runs it before it seeds anything, so a uid other than 1000 starts

workspace.why: the workspace ROOT is not in the image, so docker would create it root-owned and no build could write .gradle/, .kotlin/ or build/ into it; a named volume there is root-owned for the same reason. A tmpfs is world-writable, holds only those scratch directories, and is discarded with the container. The source binds sit inside it

filesystem.why: the image must be able to write outside the mounts. The entrypoint's fixuid repairs the passwd record before it seeds anything, so /etc is written at every start; and the warmed practice caches live under /opt, where Gradle and Maven write on every build. A read-only root filesystem, or a mount that makes one of these read-only, breaks the editor at start or breaks every graded run in it
filesystem.what_is_discarded_with_the_container: everything outside editor.mounts: the workspace root is a tmpfs and the rest of the writes are the container's own layer

mounts.purpose: the corpus's sources, and nothing else: not the repository, not $HOME
code-server's user data: the settings the entrypoint seeds once, and the reader's own edits
the Gradle user home the entrypoint seeds from the prime when it is empty; omit it when gradle is not declared
the Maven local repository the entrypoint seeds from the prime when it is empty; omit it when maven is not declared

ports.why: an unencrypted IDE with a shell. 0.0.0.0 offers it to every machine that can reach this host

environment.name: PASSWORD
environment.note: there is deliberately no default: the IDE must never start unauthenticated

environment.name: GRADLE_USER_HOME
environment.note: explicit rather than derived from $HOME, so the seeded cache and the tool agree

command_notes.bind_addr: 0.0.0.0 INSIDE the container only, which is the container's own interface; the loopback restriction is the ports entry's host_bind
command_notes.replaces_cmd: a compose command: replaces the image's CMD outright, and the image re-declares ENTRYPOINT and CMD so nothing the base bakes is appended to it
command_notes.extensions_dir: the extensions are installed into the image, not onto a volume, so an image upgrade carries them

healthcheck.why_this_interpreter: code-server's own node, which every declared set carries; a set without python has no python3 and a set without node has no node on PATH
healthcheck.ordering: a consumer whose own service creates one of the bind sources gates this one on it with depends_on: <service>: condition: service_healthy, so the editor starts after the directory exists

editor.why_no_docker_socket: spec 8.3: the Docker socket is never mounted into a serving process, not behind a flag and not only locally. This is an IDE with a shell published on a port
editor.why_restart_no: an IDE with a shell comes up when the reader asks for it, not on every boot
